overview.headline: How drag dependence is simplified into a coefficient and equation

keyPoints.point: Drag depends on density and velocity squared plus viscosity and compressibility and body size and inclination
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyPoints.point: Complex dependencies are handled by collecting effects to characterize dependence by a single variable
keyPoints.quote: One way to deal with complex dependencies is to characterize the dependence by a single variable.

keyPoints.point: Drag equation states drag equals coefficient times density times half velocity squared times reference area
keyPoints.quote: The drag equation states that drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficient includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag and induced drag components
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Dynamic pressure is density times square of velocity divided by two
keyPoints.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: variable that groups complex dependencies for calculating drag
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: area used to characterize drag dependence on body size
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: combination of density times velocity squared divided by two
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure

keyTerms.gloss: letter designating density in the drag equation
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: drag component from body shape included in the coefficient
keyTerms.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.
